title: Enforcement Decree of the Special Act on the Establishment of Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated Special City
full_text:
CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Decree is to prescribe matters delegated by the Special Act on the Establishment of Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated Special City and matters necessary for its enforcement.

CHAPTER II ESTABLISHMENT OF THE JEONNAM-GWANGJU INTEGRATED SPECIAL CITY SUPPORT COMMITTEE AND TRANSFER OF AUTHORITY, ETC.

Article 2 (Composition, etc. of the Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated Special City Support Committee)
(1) "Heads of relevant central administrative agencies prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 12(3)3 of the Special Act on the Establishment of Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated Special City (hereinafter referred to as the "Act") means the heads of the following central administrative agencies:
1. The Minister of Finance and Economy, the Minister of Science and ICT, the Minister of Education, the Minister of Justice, the Minister of National Defense, the Minister of the Interior and Safety, the Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism, the Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs, the Minister of Trade and Industry, the Minister of Health and Welfare, the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment, the Minister of Employment and Labor, the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries, the Minister of SMEs and Startups, the Minister of Planning and Budget, the Minister for Government Policy Coordination, the Minister of Government Legislation, and the Administrator of the Korea Forest Service;
2. Heads of central administrative agencies designated by the chairperson of the Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated Special City Support Committee under Article 12(1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the "Support Committee") in connection with agenda items submitted to the Support Committee.
(2) The term of office of members commissioned pursuant to Article 12(3)4 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "commissioned members") shall be two years, and they may serve only one consecutive additional term. Provided, That the term of office of a member newly commissioned due to the resignation, etc. of a commissioned member shall be the remainder of the predecessor's term.

Article 3 (Dismissal of Members)
The Prime Minister may dismiss a commissioned member in any of the following cases:
1. Where the member becomes unable to perform the duties of office for an extended period due to physical or mental infirmity or the like;
2. Where the member has committed misconduct related to the duties of office;
3. Where the member is deemed unsuitable as a member due to neglect of duties, impairment of dignity, or other reasons;
4. Where, despite falling under any of the grounds for exclusion referred to in the subparagraphs of Article 4(1), or being deemed to be in circumstances in which the fairness of the member's deliberation cannot readily be expected, the member has not recused himself or herself pursuant to paragraph (3) of that Article;
5. Where the member personally expresses that it is difficult to perform the duties of office.

Article 4 (Exclusion, Challenge, and Recusal of Members)
(1) A member of the Support Committee shall be excluded from its deliberations and resolutions in any of the following cases:
1. Where the member of the Support Committee or the member's spouse or former spouse is a party to the relevant agenda item (including officers where the party is a corporation, organization, etc.; hereinafter the same shall apply in this paragraph) or is a joint right holder or joint obligor with a party to that agenda item;
2. Where the member of the Support Committee is or was a relative of a party to the relevant agenda item;
3. Where the member of the Support Committee is performing or has performed services, advisory work, research, appraisals, or investigations relating to the relevant agenda item;
4. Where the member of the Support Committee, or the corporation, organization, etc. to which the member belongs, is or was an agent of a party to the relevant agenda item;
5. Where the member of the Support Committee is otherwise deemed to have a direct interest in the deliberations and resolutions of the Support Committee.
(2) Where a member of the Support Committee falls under any of the grounds for exclusion referred to in the subparagraphs of paragraph (1), or there are circumstances in which fair deliberations and resolutions cannot readily be expected, a party to the agenda item may file a challenge against the member with the Support Committee, and the Support Committee shall decide by resolution whether to uphold the challenge. In such cases, the member subject to the challenge shall not participate in that resolution.
(3) Where a member of the Support Committee falls under any of the grounds for exclusion referred to in the subparagraphs of paragraph (1), or considers that there are circumstances in which the fairness of his or her deliberation cannot readily be expected, the member shall voluntarily recuse himself or herself from deliberations and resolutions on the agenda item.

Article 5 (Restrictions on Qualifications for Members)
(1) None of the following persons may become a commissioned member:
1. A person who is not a national of the Republic of Korea;
2. A person falling under any of the subparagraphs of Article 33 of the State Public Officials Act;
3. A person registered as a candidate (including a preliminary candidate) in an election held pursuant to the Public Official Election Act or the Local Education Autonomy Act.
(2) Where a commissioned member comes to fall under any of the subparagraphs of paragraph (1), the Prime Minister shall dismiss the member. Provided, That the proviso to subparagraph 1 of Article 69 of the State Public Officials Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to a person falling under paragraph (1)2.

Article 6 (Duties of the Chairperson of the Support Committee)
(1) The chairperson of the Support Committee shall represent the Support Committee and oversee its affairs.
(2) Where the chairperson of the Support Committee is unable to perform the duties of office for an unavoidable reason, the relevant member shall act on the chairperson's behalf in the order of the members specified in Article 2(1)1.

Article 7 (Operation of the Support Committee)
(1) The chairperson of the Support Committee shall convene and preside over meetings of the Support Committee.
(2) A meeting of the Support Committee shall open with the attendance of a majority of the incumbent members (including members designated pursuant to Article 2(1)2) and adopt resolutions by the affirmative vote of a majority of the members present.
(3) Where deemed necessary for the efficient operation of the Support Committee, its chairperson may request the heads of relevant administrative agencies (excluding the heads of central administrative agencies under Article 2(1)), public officials, officers or employees of relevant institutions, corporations, or organizations, or private-sector experts to attend a meeting of the Support Committee and present their opinions.
(4) Except as provided in paragraphs (1) through (3), matters necessary for the operation, etc. of the Support Committee shall be determined by its chairperson following deliberation and a resolution of the Support Committee.

Article 8 (Composition and Operation of the Working Committee)
(1) The following persons shall serve as members of the working committee under Article 12(4) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the "working committee"):
1. The Vice Minister of Finance and Economy, the Vice Minister of Science and ICT, the Vice Minister of Education, the Vice Minister of Justice, the Vice Minister of National Defense, the Vice Minister of the Interior and Safety, the Vice Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism, the Vice Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs, the Vice Minister of Trade and Industry, the Vice Minister of Health and Welfare, the Vice Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment, the Vice Minister of Employment and Labor, the Vice Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, the Vice Minister of Oceans and Fisheries, the Vice Minister of SMEs and Startups, the Vice Minister of Planning and Budget, the Vice Minister for Government Policy Coordination, the Vice Minister of Government Legislation, and the Deputy Administrator of the Korea Forest Service (where the relevant institution has two or more vice ministers or deputy heads, this means one person designated by the head of that institution);
2. One of the deputy mayors of Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated Special City (hereinafter referred to as the "Integrated Special City"), designated by the Mayor of Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated Special City (hereinafter referred to as the "Integrated Special City Mayor");
3. One of the deputy superintendents of education of the Integrated Special City, designated by the Superintendent of Education of Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated Special City (hereinafter referred to as the "Integrated Special City Superintendent of Education");
4. Persons commissioned by the Minister for Government Policy Coordination from among persons with extensive knowledge and experience in urban development, local autonomy, and educational autonomy.
(2) Where necessary for the efficient operation of the working committee, expert committees for individual fields may be established and operated.
(3) Article 2(2) and Articles 3 through 7 shall apply mutatis mutandis to the terms of office, dismissal, exclusion, challenge, recusal, and restrictions on qualifications of working committee members, the duties of the chairperson of the working committee, the operation of the working committee, and other related matters. In such cases, "Prime Minister" shall be construed as "Minister for Government Policy Coordination," "Support Committee" as "working committee," and "commissioned members" as "members commissioned pursuant to Article 8(1)4."

Article 9 (Working-Level Support Group)
(1) A working-level support group shall be established within the Office for Government Policy Coordination to handle and support the affairs of the Support Committee pursuant to Article 12(6) of the Act. In such cases, where the Minister for Government Policy Coordination deems it necessary for the efficient operation of the working-level support group, the Minister may combine it with other working-level support organizations having similar functions and characteristics and establish and operate them as an integrated organization.
(2) The head of the working-level support group shall be designated by the Minister for Government Policy Coordination from among general-service public officials of the Office for Government Policy Coordination.
(3) The head of the working-level support group shall oversee its affairs and direct and supervise its staff.

Article 10 (Specialist Personnel)
Where deemed necessary to support the affairs of the Support Committee efficiently, the chairperson of the Support Committee may appoint experts in relevant fields to fixed-term public official positions in the working-level support group within budgetary limits.

Article 11 (Requests for Secondment)
Where necessary for the operation of the Support Committee or the performance of the duties of the working-level support group, the Minister for Government Policy Coordination may request the heads of relevant central administrative agencies and local governments, or the heads of public institutions under Article 4 of the Act on the Management of Public Institutions, to second their public officials, officers, or employees.

Article 12 (Commissioning of Investigations and Research, etc.)
(1) Where necessary for the efficient performance of its duties, the Support Committee may commission specialized investigations and research from relevant institutions, corporations, organizations, experts, or the like.
(2) Where necessary for the performance of its duties, the Support Committee may collect opinions on matters related to the Integrated Special City through questionnaire surveys, public hearings, seminars, or the like.

Article 13 (Allowances, etc.)
Commissioned members, working committee members commissioned pursuant to Article 8(1)4, and public officials, officers or employees of relevant institutions, corporations, or organizations, or experts attending meetings of the Support Committee or the working committee may be paid allowances, travel expenses, and other necessary expenses within budgetary limits. Provided, That allowances shall not be paid where a public official attends a meeting in direct connection with the duties under that official's jurisdiction.

Article 14 (Transfer, etc. of Affairs of Special Local Administrative Agencies)
(1) To transfer the affairs under the jurisdiction of special local administrative agencies under Article 3 of the Government Organization Act established in the former Jeollanam-do and Gwangju Metropolitan City (hereinafter referred to as "special local administrative agencies" in this Article) pursuant to Article 19(1) of the Act, the Minister of the Interior and Safety may request the heads of relevant central administrative agencies or local governments to submit necessary materials.
(2) Where the head of a central administrative agency intends to transfer affairs under the jurisdiction of a special local administrative agency to the Integrated Special City pursuant to Article 19 of the Act, the head shall hear the opinions of the Integrated Special City Mayor on the methods, scale, etc. of the transfer.
(3) Where the Integrated Special City Mayor intends to submit opinions pursuant to paragraph (2), the Mayor shall first hear the opinions of the mayors and heads of Guns and Gus having jurisdiction (the head of a Gu means the head of an autonomous Gu; hereinafter the same shall apply).

CHAPTER III AUTONOMOUS ADMINISTRATION

Article 15 (Special Cases concerning Appointment, etc. of State Public Officials)
(1) "Matters prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 40 of the Act means the following matters:
1. Authority over appointment and dismissal, disciplinary action, and other matters concerning the appointment of general-service State public officials of Grade 4 or lower;
2. Authority over appointment and dismissal, disciplinary action, and other matters concerning the appointment of research and guidance service public officials under Article 4 of the Regulations on the Appointment, etc. of Research and Guidance Service Public Officials.
(2) Where the Integrated Special City Mayor (including the chairperson of the Integrated Special City Council) intends to exercise the authority referred to in the subparagraphs of paragraph (1) pursuant to Article 40 of the Act, the Mayor shall consult with the Minister of the Interior and Safety.

Article 16 (Coordination of Metropolitan Administration)
Where the heads of relevant central administrative agencies and the Integrated Special City Mayor differ in their opinions on the formulation and implementation of plans concerning the following matters, the Prime Minister shall coordinate the matter pursuant to Article 45(1) of the Act following deliberation by the Administrative Consultation and Coordination Committee under Article 187(1) of the Local Autonomy Act:
1. Matters concerning roads, traffic, and transportation in the Integrated Special City;
2. Matters concerning the prevention of environmental pollution and environmental conservation in the Integrated Special City;
3. Matters concerning the use, conservation, development, etc. of water resources in the Integrated Special City;
4. Other matters necessary for the administration of the Integrated Special City.

Article 17 (Scope of Special Disasters)
"Disasters of a scale prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 47 of the Act means any of the following disasters:
1. Natural disasters under subparagraphs 1 and 1-2 of Article 69(1) of the Enforcement Decree of the Framework Act on the Management of Disasters and Safety;
2. Social disasters under Article 3, subparagraph 1(b) of the Framework Act on the Management of Disasters and Safety that the Integrated Special City Mayor deems to require national-level support because it is difficult to manage the disasters using only the administrative or financial capacity of the Integrated Special City;
3. Other disasters for which the Integrated Special City Mayor deems special measures at the national level necessary to effectively manage and recover from extreme damage caused by the disasters, such as large-scale human casualties or the loss of the foundations for residents' daily lives.

CHAPTER IV AUTONOMOUS FINANCE

Article 18 (Priority Support for National Policy Projects, etc.)
Where the head of a central administrative agency implements policy projects for developing regional strategic industries, expanding regional transport networks, or other policy projects deemed necessary for the Integrated Special City pursuant to Article 54(2) of the Act, the head may provide priority support to the Integrated Special City and Sis, Guns, and Gus (Gus mean autonomous Gus; hereinafter the same shall apply).

Article 19 (Budgetary Support and Special Cases)
(1) When providing various subsidies to local governments through the Special Account for Balanced Regional Development under Article 74 of the Special Act on Local Autonomy, Decentralization, and Balanced Growth or other means, the Minister of Planning and Budget may provide preferential support to the Integrated Special City pursuant to Article 56(4) of the Act.
(2) When reviewing fiscal investment and loan projects of the Integrated Special City, the head of a central administrative agency may comprehensively consider the administrative needs of the Integrated Special City and reflect them in the review pursuant to Article 56(4) of the Act.

CHAPTER V EDUCATIONAL AUTONOMY

Article 20 (Establishment of the Autonomous School Deliberative Committee)
(1) An Autonomous School Deliberative Committee shall be established under the Integrated Special City Superintendent of Education to deliberate on matters concerning the designation, operation, etc. of autonomous schools under Article 66(1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "autonomous schools").
(2) Matters necessary for the composition, operation, etc. of the Autonomous School Deliberative Committee under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by ordinance of Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated Special City (hereinafter referred to as an "Integrated Special City Ordinance") or by the education rules of the Integrated Special City.

Article 21 (Procedures for Designation of Autonomous Schools)
(1) The head of a school seeking designation as an autonomous school pursuant to Article 66(1) of the Act shall submit documents containing the following matters to the Integrated Special City Superintendent of Education:
1. The purpose and period of operation of the autonomous school;
2. The school charter;
3. The opinions of the chairperson of the board of directors of the school foundation (limited to private schools) and the head of the school;
4. Minutes of meetings of the board of directors (limited to private schools) and of the school steering committee under Article 31 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act (hereinafter referred to as the "school steering committee");
5. Other matters that the Integrated Special City Superintendent of Education deems necessary in connection with the designation and operation of autonomous schools.
(2) Where the Integrated Special City Superintendent of Education intends to designate an elementary school, middle school, high school, or special school that has submitted documents under paragraph (1) as an autonomous school, deliberation by the Autonomous School Deliberative Committee under Article 20 shall first be completed.
(3) Except as provided in paragraphs (1) and (2), matters necessary for the designation, etc. of autonomous schools shall be prescribed by the education rules of the Integrated Special City.

Article 22 (Special Cases concerning Operation of Autonomous Schools)
(1) Pursuant to Article 66(1) of the Act, the head of an autonomous school may prescribe different provisions for the following matters concerning the operation of the autonomous school. In such cases, the head shall first undergo deliberation by the school steering committee.
1. The academic year under Article 24(1) of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act;
2. Semesters and the number of school days under Article 24(4) of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act and Articles 44 and 45 of the Enforcement Decree of that Act: Provided, That where the number of school days is reduced, the reduction shall be within 20 percent of the number of school days under Article 45(1)1 of that Decree;
3. The grade system under Article 26(1) of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act;
4. The fixed number and composition ratios of school steering committee members under Article 31 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act and Articles 58 and 63 of the Enforcement Decree of that Act: Provided, That where different provisions are made for the fixed number and composition ratios of school steering committee members, the extent of adjustment shall not exceed 20 percent of the ranges for the fixed number and composition ratios of members under Article 58 of that Decree (including cases where that provision applies mutatis mutandis under Article 63(2) of that Decree).
(2) Where the Integrated Special City Superintendent of Education designates, or establishes and operates, an autonomous school pursuant to Article 66(1) and (3) of the Act, the Superintendent of Education may prescribe different provisions for the following matters within a scope that does not impair students' right to learn or educational conditions:
1. Standards for the assignment of teachers under Article 19(4) of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act (limited to cases where teachers are assigned at levels equal to or higher than those standards);
2. The durations of courses of study under Articles 39, 42, and 46 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act: Provided, That where a duration of study is reduced, the reduction shall be no more than one year for each duration of study under Articles 39, 42, and 46 of that Act.
(3) Pursuant to Article 66(1) of the Act, school rules established by the head of an autonomous school shall include the following matters:
1. Matters to be stated in school rules under Article 9(1) of the Enforcement Decree of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act;
2. Distance learning using broadcasting, information and communications media, or the like;
3. Educational activities outside school, including the operation of field training;
4. The grade system;
5. Use of textbooks;
6. Composition and operation of the school steering committee;
7. Other matters determined by the Integrated Special City Superintendent of Education.
(4) Pursuant to Article 66(1) of the Act, a person who does not possess the qualifications for a principal or vice principal under Article 21(1) of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act may be appointed as the principal or vice principal of an autonomous school.
(5) Pursuant to Article 66(1) of the Act, a person who has graduated from a junior college or has equivalent or higher educational attainment and has worked for at least five years in duties in a field related to the subject to be taught at a corporation or organization determined and publicly notified by the Integrated Special City Superintendent of Education may be appointed as an industry-academia adjunct teacher under Article 22 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act at an autonomous school, notwithstanding subparagraph 1 of attached Table 2 of the Enforcement Decree of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act.
(6) Pursuant to Article 66(1) of the Act, the head of an autonomous school may use books published in Korea or abroad as textbooks (excluding the Korean language, social studies, and moral education subjects in the curricula of elementary schools, middle schools, high schools, and special schools; hereinafter the same shall apply in this Article), in addition to textbooks under Article 29(1) of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act.
(7) Where books published in Korea or abroad are to be used as textbooks pursuant to paragraph (6), a Textbook Selection Deliberative Committee shall be established at the autonomous school to deliberate on the selection of such textbooks. In such cases, matters concerning the composition, operation, etc. of the Textbook Selection Deliberative Committee shall be determined by the head of the autonomous school.
(8) Where the head of an autonomous school requests the appointment of a teacher or deferment of the transfer of a teacher belonging to the school pursuant to Article 66(2) of the Act, the head shall obtain the consent of the teacher concerned, and the Integrated Special City Superintendent of Education shall respect the request.
(9) Except as provided in paragraphs (1) through (8), matters necessary for the operation and support of autonomous schools and other related matters shall be prescribed by the education rules of the Integrated Special City.

Article 23 (Designation, Operation, etc. of Schools for the Gifted)
(1) The head of a public or private high school seeking designation as a school for the gifted pursuant to Article 67(1) of the Act shall prepare and submit an application containing the following matters to the Integrated Special City Superintendent of Education:
1. School rules;
2. A plan for school operation;
3. A plan for operation of the curriculum;
4. A plan for conducting admissions screening;
5. A plan for the assignment of teachers;
6. Other matters determined by the Integrated Special City Superintendent of Education for the designation of schools for the gifted.
(2) Where the Integrated Special City Superintendent of Education intends to designate or establish a school for the gifted, or revoke its designation, pursuant to Article 67(1) and (2) of the Act, the Superintendent of Education shall request the consent of the Minister of Education following deliberation by the City/Do Gifted Education Promotion Committee under Article 4-3 of the Gifted Education Promotion Act (hereinafter referred to as the "City/Do Gifted Education Promotion Committee").
(3) Where the Integrated Special City Superintendent of Education intends to revoke the designation of a school for the gifted pursuant to Article 67(2) of the Act, the Superintendent of Education shall give the head of the relevant school for the gifted an opportunity to present opinions.
(4) A school for the gifted whose designation is revoked pursuant to Article 67(2) of the Act shall revert to its status before designation as a school for the gifted.
(5) Gifted education shall continue to be provided to students enrolled in the school for the gifted at the time of revocation of its designation pursuant to Article 67(2) of the Act until they graduate from that school. In such cases, the school shall be deemed a school for the gifted in relation to the students receiving gifted education.
(6) The criteria for designation and establishment of schools for the gifted designated or established by the Integrated Special City Superintendent of Education, including the numbers of classes and students and facility standards, shall be determined and publicly notified by the Integrated Special City Superintendent of Education.
(7) Except as provided in paragraphs (1) through (6), matters concerning the procedures for designation, establishment, and revocation of designation of schools for the gifted shall be determined by the Minister of Education.
(8) Foreign fixed-term teachers appointed pursuant to Article 67(5) of the Act shall satisfy any of the following qualification requirements:
1. Persons meeting the qualification standards for secondary school teachers in attached Table 2 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act;
2. Persons with at least three years of teaching experience after obtaining teaching qualifications under the laws of their home country.
(9) Foreign instructors appointed pursuant to Article 67(5) of the Act shall satisfy any of the following qualification requirements:
1. Persons falling under paragraph (8)1 or 2;
2. Persons who have obtained a bachelor's degree or higher under the laws of their home country.

Article 24 (Evaluation of Operational Performance of Schools for the Gifted)
(1) The Integrated Special City Superintendent of Education shall evaluate the operational performance of schools for the gifted every five years pursuant to the former part of Article 67(8) of the Act.
(2) For the evaluation under paragraph (1), the head of the relevant school for the gifted shall prepare and submit to the Integrated Special City Superintendent of Education a self-evaluation report containing operational performance in relation to the matters referred to in the subparagraphs of Article 23(1).
(3) The City/Do Gifted Education Promotion Committee shall deliberate on the self-evaluation report submitted pursuant to paragraph (2). In such cases, the Committee may require the head of the relevant school to submit additional necessary materials or request interviews with persons concerned.
(4) Based on the results of deliberation by the City/Do Gifted Education Promotion Committee under paragraph (3), the Integrated Special City Superintendent of Education may take the following measures as applicable:
1. Where it is deemed possible to achieve the purpose of establishment of the school for the gifted but improvements are needed: Require the formulation and implementation of an improvement plan;
2. Where it is deemed impossible to achieve the purpose of establishment of the school for the gifted: Revoke its designation pursuant to Article 67(2) of the Act.
(5) Except as provided in paragraphs (1) through (4), matters necessary for the evaluation of operational performance, disclosure of evaluation results, and other related matters shall be separately determined by the Integrated Special City Superintendent of Education in consultation with the Minister of Education.

Article 25 (Operation of Special-Purpose High Schools)
(1) "Schools aimed at specialized education in special fields prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 68(1) of the Act means the high schools referred to in the subparagraphs of Article 90(1) of the Enforcement Decree of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act.
(2) Foreign fixed-term teachers appointed pursuant to Article 68(3) of the Act shall satisfy any of the qualification requirements referred to in the subparagraphs of Article 23(8).
(3) Foreign instructors appointed pursuant to Article 68(3) of the Act shall satisfy any of the qualification requirements referred to in the subparagraphs of Article 23(9).

Article 26 (Special Cases concerning Integrated Operation of Schools)
(1) "Schools of a size not exceeding that prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 69(1) of the Act means schools determined by the Integrated Special City Superintendent of Education, taking into consideration the characteristics and conditions of the region and the schools and other relevant factors, from among schools with no more than 200 enrolled students (limited to schools under Article 2 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act).
(2) The Integrated Special City Superintendent of Education shall establish and operate relevant training courses to ensure the professional competence of teachers wishing to work at schools under Article 69(1) of the Act and teachers intending to perform cross-teaching under paragraph (2) of that Article.

Article 27 (Admission to Middle Schools Operating Distinctive Curricula)
Pursuant to Article 70(2) of the Act, the Integrated Special City Superintendent of Education may determine matters necessary for admission, re-enrollment, school transfer, and transfer admission to middle schools operating distinctive curricula under paragraph (1) of that Article for the following persons:
1. Children or students who are members of multicultural families under Article 2, subparagraph 1 of the Multicultural Families Support Act;
2. Children or students who are foreigners residing in Korea;
3. Other persons recognized by the Integrated Special City Superintendent of Education as children or students consistent with the purposes of operating the distinctive curricula.

Article 28 (Criteria, etc. for Establishment of Attached Special Schools)
(1) A special school established by the Integrated Special City Superintendent of Education attached to an elementary school, middle school, or high school pursuant to Article 70(4) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as an "attached special school") shall have at least six classes.
(2) Articles 3 through 5 of the Decree on Standards for Special School Facilities and Equipment shall apply mutatis mutandis to standards for the facilities and equipment of attached special schools.
(3) The standard area of the school site of an attached special school shall be determined by the Integrated Special City Superintendent of Education, taking into consideration the number of students, the scale of facilities necessary for the operation of the curriculum, the area of the school site of the school to which the special school is attached, local conditions, the educational environment, and other relevant factors. In such cases, detailed criteria for the standard area of school sites shall be prescribed by the education rules of the Integrated Special City.
(4) Where a special school is established attached to another school pursuant to Article 70(4) of the Act, certain facilities and equipment, such as sports grounds, auditoriums, and cafeterias, may be shared with the elementary school, middle school, or high school for the smooth operation of the curriculum and administrative efficiency, within a scope that does not interfere with students' educational activities or safety. In such cases, the scope of facilities and equipment that may be shared and matters necessary for their operation shall be determined and publicly notified by the Integrated Special City Superintendent of Education.
(5) The school levels of attached special schools and of the elementary schools, middle schools, or high schools to which they are attached shall be determined by the Integrated Special City Superintendent of Education, taking into consideration students' ages and developmental characteristics, the operation of the curriculum, and other relevant factors.
(6) Except as provided in paragraphs (1) through (5), detailed matters necessary for the establishment, etc. of attached special schools shall be determined by the Integrated Special City Superintendent of Education within the scope of relevant statutes and regulations.

Article 29 (Areas Where Foreign Educational Institutions May Be Established)
(1) Pursuant to Article 73(1) of the Act, the Integrated Special City Mayor may designate and publicly notify areas deemed necessary for the promotion of foreign investment, creation of an international educational environment, improvement of settlement conditions for foreigners, or other related purposes as areas where foreign educational institutions (meaning foreign educational institutions under Article 2, subparagraph 5 of the Special Act on Designation and Management of Free Economic Zones; hereinafter the same shall apply) may be established.
(2) Where the Integrated Special City Mayor intends to change an area designated and publicly notified pursuant to paragraph (1) (limited to areas where foreign educational institutions corresponding to schools at the high school level or below may be established), the Mayor shall first consult with the Integrated Special City Superintendent of Education.

Article 30 (Support, etc. for Foreign Educational Institutions)
(1) A foreign educational institution seeking financial support or provision of a site from the State or the Integrated Special City pursuant to Article 73(8) of the Act shall apply to the Integrated Special City Mayor by stating its operational purpose in an application for support.
(2) Upon receiving an application under paragraph (1), the Integrated Special City Mayor may, where necessary, request the relevant support from the head of the central administrative agency having jurisdiction, and the head of the central administrative agency receiving the request may subsidize a portion of the funding or provide a site.
(3) A foreign educational institution that receives support under paragraph (2) shall not use the subsidy or site for any purpose other than the purpose for which it was supported or provided.
(4) Except as provided in paragraphs (1) through (3), matters necessary for support by the Integrated Special City for foreign educational institutions shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City Ordinance.

Article 31 (Ratio of Korean National Students at Foreign Educational Institutions)
"Ratio prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 73(9) of the Act means a ratio adjusted by the committee under the Integrated Special City Superintendent of Education pursuant to paragraph (5) of that Article within a range of up to 50 percent of the authorized student capacity of the relevant foreign educational institution. Provided, That the Integrated Special City Superintendent of Education may, taking into consideration the educational conditions of the Integrated Special City, further increase the admission ratio for Korean national students adjusted by the committee, within the student capacity, by the education rules of the Integrated Special City.

Article 32 (Special Cases Concerning the Training of Personnel for Regional Development)
(1) Matters concerning support for training talented personnel, encouraging their settlement in the region, and creating conditions for settlement under Article 75(1) and (2) of the Act shall be as prescribed by Integrated Special City Ordinance within the scope of the following:
1. Eligible persons: Talented personnel, such as elementary, middle, and high school students in the region; students and graduates of universities in the region; jobseekers; persons employed by businesses, research institutions, and public institutions in the region; persons working in public service fields, such as medical care and education; and specialized personnel moving into the region from other regions or abroad;
2. Methods: Administrative and financial support by the Integrated Special City, such as scholarships and student financial aid, research support, support for education and training expenses, employment and business start-up support, and support for creating conditions for settlement, such as housing, educational, and cultural facilities;
3. Other matters that the Integrated Special City Mayor deems necessary for support for training talented personnel, encouraging their settlement in the region, and creating conditions for settlement.
(2) The Integrated Special City Mayor shall formulate the policies under Article 75(1) and (2) of the Act in accordance with the procedures for establishing and implementing the Si/Do master plan under Article 5 of the Act on the Development of Local Universities and Colleges and Regional Human Resources and the Si/Do implementation plan under Article 6 of that Act, and shall also incorporate their contents into the relevant Si/Do master plan and implementation plan.
(3) Where the policies under Article 75(1) and (2) of the Act relate to the duties of the superintendent of education prescribed in the Local Education Autonomy Act, the Integrated Special City Mayor shall consult with the Integrated Special City Superintendent of Education in advance.

Article 33 (Procedures for Requesting Application of Special Cases Concerning the Operation of High Schools Tailored to Industrial Demand, Etc.)
Where the Integrated Special City Mayor or the Integrated Special City Superintendent of Education intends to request the application of special cases concerning the operation of a high school tailored to industrial demand or a specialized high school pursuant to Article 82(3) of the Act, they shall consult with each other in advance on the relevant matters.

Article 34 (Operation of Linked Curricula among Educational Institutions and Industrial Enterprises)
(1) The linked curricula under Article 82(5) of the Act may be jointly developed and operated by high schools tailored to industrial demand or specialized high schools together with universities, research institutions, and industrial enterprises.
(2) The linked curricula under paragraph (1) may include the following matters:
1. Joint development of subjects or courses linked to regional strategic industry fields;
2. Operation of field training, research project classes, and practical education programs;
3. Cooperation in classes by relevant experts from universities, research institutions, industrial enterprises, etc.;
4. Other matters necessary for training specialized personnel in fields of regional specialization.

Article 35 (Allocation of Responsibilities among Relevant Institutions for Training Talent in Regional Strategic Industry Fields, Etc.)
(1) For the operation of high schools tailored to industrial demand or specialized high schools in regional strategic industry fields (hereinafter in this Article referred to as "schools") and their curricula, the Integrated Special City Mayor and the Integrated Special City Superintendent of Education may, pursuant to Article 82(6) of the Act, request cooperation or allocation of responsibilities from the Integrated Special City Mayor, the Integrated Special City Superintendent of Education, and the heads of relevant institutions, such as universities, research institutions, and industrial enterprises, for the matters specified in the following classifications:
1. Integrated Special City Mayor: Administrative and financial support for training talent in regional strategic industry fields;
2. Integrated Special City Superintendent of Education:
(a) Development and approval of school curricula for training talent in regional strategic industry fields;
(b) Strengthening links between school education, such as vocational education and career education, and industrial workplaces;
(c) Support for the operation of educational cooperation programs between schools and universities, research institutions, and industrial enterprises;
3. Universities:
(a) Development and operation of curricula reflecting regional strategic industry demand;
(b) Joint research and technology transfer at regional industrial innovation campuses under Article 82(4) of the Act;
(c) Strengthening links between higher education and lifelong education and strengthening industry-academia-research cooperation;
4. Research institutions and industrial enterprises:
(a) Support for education based on industrial workplaces, such as field training, job training, and employment linkages;
(b) Dispatch of relevant experts from industrial enterprises as instructors;
(c) Joint use of educational facilities and equipment and operation of programs linked to recruitment.
(2) The Integrated Special City Mayor and the Integrated Special City Superintendent of Education may jointly establish and operate a consultative body with participation by relevant institutions to promote the training of talent in regional strategic industry fields and industry-academia-research cooperation.
(3) Matters necessary for the composition and operation of the consultative body under paragraph (2) may be prescribed by Integrated Special City Ordinance.

Chapter VI Development and Establishment of Foundations for the Capital of Artificial Intelligence, Energy, and Culture

Section 1 Urban Development

Article 36 (Special Cases Concerning Deliberation on Spatial Restructuring Plans)
The term "matters prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as changes to spatial restructuring plans decided by the Integrated Special City Mayor" in Article 103 of the Act means changes concerning the matters under Article 35-6(2)1(b) of the National Land Planning and Utilization Act, excluding the following:
1. Changes to the purposes of designation of the specific-use zones under the subparagraphs of Article 35-2(1) of the National Land Planning and Utilization Act;
2. Other material changes prescribed by the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport in consultation with the Integrated Special City Mayor.

Article 37 (Delegation of Authority Concerning Public Housing District Development Projects)
The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport shall delegate the following powers to the Integrated Special City Mayor pursuant to Article 106(2) of the Act:
1. Designation or modification of housing districts, or withdrawal of their designation, under Article 6(1) of the Special Act on Public Housing;
2. Periodic surveys and fact-finding surveys under Article 9(5) of the Special Act on Public Housing;
3. Public notice of designation or modification of housing districts, or withdrawal of their designation, under Article 12(1) of the Special Act on Public Housing;
4. Approval of district plans under Article 17(1) of the Special Act on Public Housing (including approval of changes) and public notice of district plans under paragraph (3) of that Article;
5. Completion inspections under Article 31(1) of the Special Act on Public Housing and public announcement of completion inspections under paragraph (2) of that Article. In such cases, "Official Gazette" in that paragraph shall be construed as "official bulletin of the Integrated Special City".

Article 38 (Consultation for Approval of Public Housing District Development Projects)
(1) A public housing project operator under Article 106(2) of the Act shall submit to the Integrated Special City Mayor a public housing district development project plan that includes the matters specified in the subparagraphs of Article 17(1) of the Special Act on Public Housing, accompanied by the documents specified in the subparagraphs of Article 16(2) of the Enforcement Decree of that Act.
(2) Where the Integrated Special City Mayor intends to approve a public housing district development project plan submitted under paragraph (1), the Mayor shall consult with the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport and the heads of relevant central administrative agencies pursuant to Article 106(3) of the Act. In such cases, the consultation period shall not exceed 20 days, but may be extended only once by up to 10 days at the request of the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport and the heads of relevant central administrative agencies.

Article 39 (Subsidies or Loans to Passenger Motor Vehicle Transport Platform Business Operators)
(1) The projects eligible for subsidies or loans under Article 130(2) of the Act shall be as follows:
1. Projects to establish and upgrade transport platforms under subparagraph 7 of Article 2 of the Passenger Transport Service Act;
2. Projects to expand and improve common facilities or safety management facilities for passenger safety.
(2) A passenger motor vehicle transport platform business operator (meaning a person operating the businesses under the subparagraphs of Article 49-2 of the Passenger Transport Service Act) intending to receive a subsidy or loan under Article 130(2) of the Act shall submit to the Integrated Special City Mayor an application stating the following matters:
1. The address and name of the applicant (in the case of a corporation, meaning its name and the name of its representative);
2. The type of passenger motor vehicle transport platform business, the permission, license, or registration number, and its date;
3. The reason for seeking the subsidy or loan;
4. The amount of the subsidy or loan sought.
(3) The application under paragraph (2) shall be accompanied by the following documents:
1. A project plan stating the purpose, implementation plan, effects, facilities, etc. of the project for which the subsidy or loan is sought;
2. A plan for the use of the subsidy or loan funds.
(4) The Integrated Special City Mayor shall submit to the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport the documents submitted under paragraphs (2) and (3), together with materials reviewing their appropriateness and feasibility.

Article 40 (Subsidies for Costs of Locally Managed Ports)
(1) Where the Integrated Special City Mayor intends to receive a subsidy pursuant to Article 136(1) of the Act, the Mayor shall apply for the inclusion of the subsidy in the budget pursuant to Article 4 of the Subsidy Management Act.
(2) In response to an application for a subsidy under paragraph (1), the Government may subsidize part of the necessary costs for the Integrated Special City Mayor from the national treasury, within the limits of the budget and pursuant to the Subsidy Management Act.

Article 41 (Special Cases Concerning Station Area Development)
Pursuant to Article 139(2) of the Act, the Integrated Special City Mayor may prescribe different building coverage ratios and floor area ratios for a development area within limits not exceeding 150/100 of the building coverage ratios and floor area ratios applicable in the relevant specific-use area under Articles 77 and 78 of the National Land Planning and Utilization Act (where the specific-use area is changed pursuant to Article 139(1) of the Act, the building coverage ratios and floor area ratios applicable in the changed specific-use area shall serve as the basis).

Article 42 (Support Measures for Relocating Employees and Their Families)
(1) The head of a relocating public institution under subparagraph 2 of Article 2 of the Special Act on the Creation and Development of Innovation Cities (hereinafter in this Article referred to as a "relocating public institution") may prepare and implement support measures for relocating employees and their families that include the following matters pursuant to Article 144(3) of the Act:
1. Matters concerning payment of moving expenses to relocating employees at the level of actual costs (expenses actually incurred);
2. Matters concerning payment of temporary relocation allowances to relocating employees;
3. Other matters deemed necessary for the stable settlement of relocating employees and their families.
(2) The specific eligible persons, methods, procedures, and other matters necessary for support under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by the head of the relocating public institution.
(3) The head of a relocating public institution shall establish a cooperation system with the Integrated Special City and the Integrated Special City Office of Education so that children relocating together with employees have no difficulties with school transfer and enrollment or the use of childcare facilities.

Section 2 Promotion of Industry

Article 43 (Establishment of Master Plans, Etc.)
(1) The Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated Special City master plan under Article 150(1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the "master plan") shall be established every 10 years.
(2) Where the Integrated Special City Mayor intends to establish a master plan, the Mayor shall prepare a draft master plan, publicly announce its main contents in a daily newspaper, an official bulletin, the Integrated Special City's website, etc., and make it available for public inspection for at least 14 days.
(3) A person with an opinion on the draft master plan publicly announced under paragraph (2) may submit a written opinion to the Integrated Special City Mayor during the inspection period.
(4) Upon receipt of a written opinion under paragraph (3), the Integrated Special City Mayor shall prepare a written assessment of the opinion and notify the submitter of that assessment or disclose it on the Integrated Special City's website, etc.
(5) The term "minor matters prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the proviso to Article 150(5) of the Act means any of the following matters:
1. A change in the area of each development project (meaning a development project implemented pursuant to the master plan; hereinafter the same shall apply in this Article and Article 44) within a range not exceeding 10/100 of its originally planned area;
2. A change in the plan resulting from the establishment, modification, abolition, etc. of airports, ports, roads, water supply facilities, basic environmental facilities, etc. whose project plans have been finalized under other Acts;
3. Addition or discontinuation of projects within a scope that does not change the objectives of each development project;
4. A change in a detailed project plan, such as a change in the business type of the relevant development project, within a scope that does not change the objectives of each development project.

Article 44 (Development Project Implementers)
(1) The term "public institutions prescribed by Presidential Decree" in subparagraph 2 of Article 155 of the Act means the following public institutions:
1. The Korea Land and Housing Corporation under the Korea Land and Housing Corporation Act;
2. The Korea Water Resources Corporation under the Korea Water Resources Corporation Act;
3. The Korea Rural Community Corporation under the Korea Rural Community Corporation and Farmland Management Fund Act;
4. The Korea Tourism Organization under the Korea Tourism Organization Act;
5. The Korea Railroad Corporation under the Korea Railroad Corporation Act;
6. The Korea Airports Corporation under the Korea Airports Corporation Act.
(2) The term "government-funded institutions prescribed by Presidential Decree" in subparagraph 3 of Article 155 of the Act means the Korea National Railway under the Korea National Railway Act (limited to cases where it implements a station area development project under subparagraph 2 of Article 2 of the Act on the Development and Use of Station Areas).

Article 45 (Designation of Investment Promotion Districts)
(1) The term "investment meeting or exceeding the standards prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 164(1) of the Act means any of the following investments:
1. Investment of at least 500 million won, with at least 10 regular employees, for the new installation of facilities for operating any of the following businesses:
(a) Research and development business under the Korean Standard Industrial Classification publicly notified by the Head of the National Data Agency pursuant to Article 22 of the Statistics Act;
(b) Research and development business concerning nanotechnology under subparagraph 1 of Article 2 of the Nanotechnology Development Promotion Act;
(c) Research and development business concerning health and medical technology under Article 2(1)1 of the Health and Medical Technology Promotion Act;
(d) Business concerning the research industry under item (b) of subparagraph 1 of Article 2 of the Research Industry Promotion Act;
2. Investment of at least 1 billion won, with at least 15 regular employees, for the new installation of facilities for operating any of the following businesses:
(a) Complex logistics terminal business under subparagraph 4 of Article 2 of the Act on the Development and Operation of Logistics Facilities;
(b) Business developing and operating joint collection and delivery centers under subparagraph 16 of Article 2 of the Distribution Industry Development Act;
(c) Business operating port facilities under subparagraph 5 of Article 2 of the Harbor Act and logistics industry business operated in port hinterland complexes under subparagraph 11 of that Article;
3. Investment of at least 2 billion won, with at least 30 regular employees, for the new installation of facilities for operating any of the following businesses:
(a) Any of the following businesses under the Korean Standard Industrial Classification publicly notified by the Head of the National Data Agency pursuant to Article 22 of the Statistics Act:
    1) Manufacturing;
    2) Telecommunications;
    3) Computer programming, system integration, and management;
    4) Information services and other scientific and technological services;
    5) Production of motion pictures, videos, and broadcast programs; services related to the production of motion pictures, videos, and broadcast programs; operation of sound recording facilities; and publishing of music and other audio materials;
    6) Development and supply of game software;
    7) Operation of performance facilities, performing arts groups, and other services related to creative activities and the arts;
(b) Engineering business under subparagraph 3 of Article 2 of the Engineering Industry Promotion Act;
(c) Aerospace industry under subparagraph 1 of Article 2 of the Aerospace Industry Development Promotion Act;
(d) Track transportation business under subparagraph 7 of Article 2 of the Track Transportation Act;
(e) Business generating electricity using new energy or renewable energy under subparagraph 1 or 2 of Article 2 of the Act on the Promotion of the Development, Use and Diffusion of New and Renewable Energy;
(f) Tourist hotel business, floating tourist hotel business, or Korean traditional hotel business under Article 2(1)2(a) through (c) of the Enforcement Decree of the Tourism Promotion Act: Provided, That cases involving the operation of a casino business under Article 3(1)5 of the Tourism Promotion Act or a bonded sales outlet under Article 196 of the Customs Act shall be excluded;
(g) Specialized resort business, comprehensive resort business, tourist excursion boat business, or tourist performance venue business under Article 2(1)3(a), (b), (d), or (e) of the Enforcement Decree of the Tourism Promotion Act: Provided, That, in the case of specialized resort businesses and comprehensive resort businesses, cases involving the operation of a resort condominium business under Article 3(1)2(b) of the Tourism Promotion Act or a golf course business under Article 10(1)1 of the Installation and Utilization of Sports Facilities Act shall be excluded;
(h) International conference facility business under Article 2(1)4(a) of the Enforcement Decree of the Tourism Promotion Act;
(i) Comprehensive theme park business under Article 2(1)5(a) of the Enforcement Decree of the Tourism Promotion Act;
(j) Tourist restaurant business under Article 2(1)6(d) of the Enforcement Decree of the Tourism Promotion Act;
(k) Marina business under subparagraph 5 of Article 2 of the Act on the Development and Management of Marinas;
(l) Business operating welfare facilities for older persons under Article 31 of the Senior Citizens Welfare Act;
(m) Business operating youth training facilities under subparagraph 1 of Article 10 of the Youth Activity Promotion Act;
(n) Business operating an educational institute under item (b) of subparagraph 10 of Attached Table 1 to the Enforcement Decree of the Building Act.
(2) The term "areas meeting the conditions prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 164(2)2 of the Act means areas meeting all of the following conditions:
1. A district-unit plan under subparagraph 5 of Article 2 of the National Land Planning and Utilization Act shall have been determined for the area;
2. The State, a local government, a public institution under Article 4 of the Act on the Management of Public Institutions, or a local public corporation established pursuant to Article 49 of the Local Public Enterprises Act shall implement a development project for the entire area under subparagraph 1;
3. The project implementer under subparagraph 2 shall have secured ownership or rights of use over at least two-thirds of the land in the relevant area.

Article 46 (Criteria for Withdrawal of Designation of Investment Promotion Districts)
The term "where the criteria prescribed by Presidential Decree are no longer met" in Article 165(1) of the Act means any of the following cases:
1. Where investment has not been completed within 10 years from the date of public notice under Article 164(3) of the Act: Provided, That the period shall be 5 years where the investment promotion district was designated because it falls under paragraph (2)1 of that Article;
2. Where the purpose of designation as an investment promotion district cannot be achieved or is expected not to be achieved due to substantial lack of progress in investment, etc.;
3. Where it is expected that the investment promotion district cannot be developed within a reasonable period due to restrictions on development activities under other statutes and regulations, investors' reluctance to participate in the project, etc.

Article 47 (Criteria and Procedures for Financial Support for Investment Promotion Districts)
The criteria and procedures for financial support provided by the State pursuant to Article 166(1) of the Act shall be prescribed by the head of the competent central administrative agency following deliberation by the Support Committee, taking into comprehensive consideration the following matters:
1. The scale of investment attracted;
2. The scale of job creation;
3. Effects on technology development in regionally specialized industries;
4. Effects on attracting advanced industries or leading enterprises in specialized fields;
5. Other contributions to balanced development and the regional economy.

Article 48 (Lease of State Property, Etc.)
(1) Where land, factories, or other State property owned by the State (hereinafter in this Article referred to as "property, etc.") is made subject, under a negotiated contract, to permission for use and profit-making or to a lease (hereinafter in this Article collectively referred to as a "lease"), the rent shall be an amount calculated by multiplying the value (monetary value) of the relevant property, etc. by a rate of at least 10/1,000 pursuant to Article 167(4) of the Act.
(2) The heads of central government agencies, etc. under subparagraph 11 of Article 2 of the State Property Act (hereinafter in this Article referred to as the "heads of central government agencies, etc.") may, pursuant to Article 167(5) of the Act, postpone the payment due date for the purchase price of property, etc. owned by the State for up to 1 year, or allow payment in installments over up to 20 years with interest at a rate of less than 4 percent per year.
(3) Where the heads of central government agencies, etc. lease property, etc. owned by the State to tenant enterprises, they may grant a reduction of or exemption from rent within a limit of 75/100 of the rent pursuant to Article 167(6) of the Act.
(4) A person intending to obtain a reduction of or exemption from rent for property, etc. owned by the State pursuant to Article 167(6) of the Act shall apply for the reduction or exemption to the heads of central government agencies, etc.

Article 49 (Policies to Promote Relocation to Investment Promotion Districts)
To promote the relocation of enterprises to investment promotion districts pursuant to Article 168(1) of the Act, the State may establish policies that include the following matters following deliberation by the Support Committee:
1. Types of enterprises targeted for relocation;
2. The basic direction of policies to support relocating enterprises;
3. Measures to promote enterprise relocation;
4. Support measures, such as subsidies, for enterprise relocation;
5. Expected effects of the relocation of the enterprises targeted for relocation;
6. Other matters deemed necessary by the chairperson of the Support Committee.

Article 50 (Special Cases Concerning Designation of Special Research and Development Zones)
Where the Minister of Science and ICT designates a special research and development zone in the Integrated Special City pursuant to Article 169(2) of the Act by the method under Article 5(1)1 of the Enforcement Decree of the Special Act on the Promotion of Special Research and Development Zones, the Minister may, notwithstanding paragraph (2)1(a) of that Article, designate the area as a special research and development zone if the area proposed for designation contains at least 40 research institutions in science and technology fields, including at least 2 national research institutions or government-funded research institutions [including branches (branch institutes)].

Article 51 (Methods and Procedures for Evaluating the Operational Performance of Special Cases Concerning Environmental Impact Assessments, Etc.)
(1) When evaluating the operational performance, etc. of the special cases under Articles 172 and 173 of the Act pursuant to Article 174(2) of the Act (hereinafter in this Article referred to as "performance evaluation"), the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall establish an evaluation plan that includes the following matters (hereinafter in this Article referred to as an "evaluation plan"). In such cases, the Minister may hear the opinion of the Integrated Special City Mayor on the evaluation plan.
1. The basic direction of performance evaluation;
2. Performance evaluation methods;
3. Performance evaluation procedures;
4. Other matters necessary for performance evaluation.
(2) Where the collection and analysis of materials, etc. is necessary to establish an evaluation plan, the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment may commission surveys, research, etc. from specialized institutions related to evaluation, etc., or hear the opinions of experts.
(3) The Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall notify the Integrated Special City Mayor of the evaluation plan no later than 1 year before the notification deadline under Article 174(2) of the Act.
(4) To conduct performance evaluation objectively and efficiently, the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment may establish and operate an evaluation team consisting of the following persons (hereinafter in this Article referred to as the "evaluation team"). In such cases, the Minister may designate 1 member under subparagraph 3 or 4 as the team leader to oversee the duties of the evaluation team under paragraph (5).
1. For each of the special cases under Articles 172 and 173 of the Act, 1 official of the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment responsible for duties related to that special case;
2. 1 official of a regional environmental office with jurisdiction over the Integrated Special City;
3. 8 experts recognized as having extensive expertise and experience in consultations related to the special cases under Articles 172 and 173 of the Act (including 3 persons recommended by the Integrated Special City Mayor);
4. 2 experts recognized as having extensive expertise and experience in local autonomy, decentralization, and balanced regional development (including 1 person recommended by the Integrated Special City Mayor).
(5) The evaluation team shall perform the following duties in relation to performance evaluation:
1. Support for conducting performance evaluation in accordance with the evaluation plan;
2. Preparation of a report consolidating performance evaluation results;
3. Hearing and coordinating the opinions of the Integrated Special City Mayor in relation to the performance of the duties under subparagraphs 1 and 2.
(6) Where necessary for performance evaluation, the evaluation team may conduct on-site inspections, interviews with relevant persons, etc.
(7) Based on the report under paragraph (5)2, the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall comprehensively review whether to extend or abolish the time limit for the special cases under Articles 172 and 173 of the Act, matters concerning improvements to the system, etc., and then notify the Integrated Special City Mayor of the performance evaluation results and opinions on measures to be taken.
(8) The evaluation team shall be deemed to have completed its duties and to have been dissolved when the evaluation results and opinions on measures to be taken have been notified to the Integrated Special City Mayor pursuant to paragraph (7).

Article 52 (Delegation of Authority Concerning Specialized Complexes for National Advanced Strategic Industries)
For the efficient development and operation of strategic industry specialized complexes designated pursuant to Article 16 of the Act on Special Measures for Strengthening and Protecting the Competitiveness of National Advanced Strategic Industries within the jurisdiction of the Integrated Special City (hereinafter referred to as "specialized complexes"), the Minister of Trade and Industry shall delegate the following powers to the Integrated Special City Mayor pursuant to Article 186(2) of the Act:
1. Authority concerning the execution and management of budgets provided by the State to local governments in relation to the development and operation of specialized complexes. In such cases, the procedures prescribed in budget-related statutes and regulations, such as the National Finance Act, shall be observed;
2. Authority to consult and coordinate with the heads of relevant administrative agencies for the prompt processing of authorizations, permissions, approvals, consultations, etc. related to the development and operation of specialized complexes (including consultation on authorizations, permissions, etc. under Article 19 of the Act on Special Measures for Strengthening and Protecting the Competitiveness of National Advanced Strategic Industries).

Article 53 (Support for Industrial Complex Infrastructure)
The term "infrastructure prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as roads and railways" in Article 194 of the Act means the following facilities:
1. Railways included in the national railway network construction plan under Article 4 of the Act on the Construction of Railways and the Maintenance and Management of Railway Facilities;
2. Roads included in the road construction and management plan under Article 6 of the Road Act;
3. Facilities under the subparagraphs of Article 27(1) of the Enforcement Decree of the Industrial Sites and Development Act.

Article 54 (Scale of Current Transactions Payable by External Means of Payment)
The term "current transactions not exceeding the scale prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 211 of the Act means current transactions of no more than 20,000 United States dollars per transaction.

Article 55 (Special Cases Concerning the Immigration Act)
The term "districts and complexes prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 213 of the Act means districts or complexes falling under any of the following:
1. Industrial complexes under subparagraph 8 of Article 2 of the Industrial Sites and Development Act;
2. Specialized complexes;
3. Investment promotion districts under Article 164 of the Act;
4. Smart agriculture promotion districts under Article 279 of the Act;
5. Cultural districts under Article 351 of the Act and cultural industry promotion districts under Article 28-2(1) of the Framework Act on the Promotion of Cultural Industries.

Article 56 (Provision of Foreign-Language Services, Etc.)
(1) In principle, English shall be the foreign language used for the foreign-language services under Article 216(1) of the Act, but other foreign languages may be used where deemed necessary.
(2) The scope of foreign-language services under Article 216(1) of the Act shall be as follows:
1. Statutes and regulations related to the development of the Integrated Special City (including ordinances and rules);
2. The master plan and related detailed project implementation plans established and prepared by the Integrated Special City;
3. Various operational manuals and guidance materials prepared by the Integrated Special City in relation to approval of the implementation of development projects under Article 156 of the Act;
4. Responding to inquiries, handling grievances, and providing consultation for civil petitioners, such as foreign investors, in relation to development projects;
5. Various public announcements, public notices, and notifications made pursuant to the Act and this Decree;
6. Other matters deemed necessary for the convenience of foreign investors.
(3) At the request of foreign investors, etc., the Integrated Special City Mayor shall translate into English and provide materials related to the subparagraphs of paragraph (2), and shall provide interpretation services where necessary.
(4) To provide foreign-language services under paragraph (2), the Integrated Special City Mayor shall assign specialized personnel necessary for foreign investment, etc., or prepare and keep relevant materials, etc.
(5) At the request of civil petitioners, such as foreign investors, the Integrated Special City Mayor may provide support for handling civil petitions, including the preparation and submission of application documents.

Article 57 (Designation of Specialized Industries for Si/Gun/Gu)
(1) Pursuant to Article 217(1) of the Act, the Integrated Special City Mayor shall designate at least 1 specialized industry for each Si/Gun/Gu upon application by the head of the Si/Gun/Gu or on the Mayor's own initiative.
(2) Where the Integrated Special City Mayor intends to designate or change specialized industries for each Si/Gun/Gu pursuant to Article 217(1) of the Act, the Mayor shall consider the following matters:
1. The regional industrial structure and degree of business concentration;
2. Regional resources and the foundation of related industries;
3. The scale of participation and growth potential of local small and medium enterprises;
4. Links with policies for promoting regionally specialized industries under Article 6(2)6 of the Act on the Development of Local Small and Medium Enterprises and Promotion of Innovation, Etc.;
5. Job creation and spillover effects on the regional economy;
6. Other matters necessary for promoting specialized industries for Si/Gun/Gu.
(3) Where the Integrated Special City Mayor intends to designate or change specialized industries, the Mayor may hear the opinions of the heads of relevant central administrative agencies, including the Minister of SMEs and Startups, and of Si/Gun/Gu, universities, research institutions, industrial enterprises, etc.

Article 58 (Establishment of Support Plans for Specialized Industries for Si/Gun/Gu)
(1) A support plan for specialized industries for each Si/Gun/Gu under Article 217(2) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as a "support plan") shall include the following matters:
1. Objectives and implementation strategies for promoting specialized industries;
2. Measures for developing local small and medium enterprises and creating an industrial ecosystem;
3. Measures to support technology development, commercialization, business growth, and investment attraction;
4. Measures for industry-academia-research cooperation and links with project implementers, etc. under Article 4 of the Act on Special Cases concerning Support for Industrial Technology Complexes;
5. Financing and investment plans;
6. Performance management and evaluation measures;
7. Other matters necessary for promoting specialized industries for Si/Gun/Gu.
(2) When establishing a support plan, the Integrated Special City Mayor may link it with the promotion plan under Article 6(1) of the Act on the Development of Local Small and Medium Enterprises and Promotion of Innovation, Etc.

Article 59 (Support for and Promotion of Specialized Industries, etc.)
(1) The Integrated Special City Mayor may undertake the following projects to promote specialized industries of Si/Gun/Gu pursuant to Article 217 (2) of the Act:
1. Support for research and development and technology commercialization;
2. Development of industrial complexes and infrastructure;
3. Support for start-ups and business growth;
4. Training of specialized personnel and education and training;
5. Support for attracting investment and businesses;
6. Support for industry-academia-research cooperation and joint research;
7. Support for developing sales channels and exports;
8. Other projects necessary to promote specialized industries of Si/Gun/Gu.
(2) The Integrated Special City Mayor shall regularly evaluate the performance of projects supporting specialized industries pursuant to Article 217 (2) of the Act.
(3) The results of evaluations under paragraph (2) may be reflected in adjustments to support plans and in budgets.
(4) The heads of relevant central administrative agencies, including the Minister of SMEs and Startups, may select projects or regions eligible for support and provide support within budgetary limits to promote and support specialized industries in each Si/Gun/Gu pursuant to Article 217 (3) of the Act.

Article 60 (Entrustment of Operation of the Jeonnam-Gwangju Small and Medium Enterprise Welfare Center)
"Specialized institutions prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 220 (5) of the Act means the following corporations or organizations:
1. Public institutions under Article 4 of the Act on the Management of Public Institutions;
2. Local public corporations under Article 49 of the Local Public Enterprises Act and local public agencies under Article 76 of that Act;
3. Non-profit corporations under Article 32 of the Civil Act that have a record of performing affairs in the fields of support for small and medium enterprises, worker welfare, or the local economy and possess specialized personnel and other necessary resources;
4. Non-profit non-governmental organizations under Article 2 of the Assistance for Non-Profit, Non-Governmental Organizations Act that are related to the promotion of worker welfare.

Article 61 (Support for Creating Energy Self-Sufficient Cities)
"Projects prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as distributed energy businesses under the Special Act on the Promotion of Distributed Energy and the establishment of smart grids under Article 2, subparagraph 2 of the Act on the Establishment and Promotion of Use of Smart Grids" in Article 228 (2) of the Act means the following projects:
1. Distributed energy businesses under Article 2, subparagraph 2 of the Special Act on the Promotion of Distributed Energy conducted within specialized distributed energy areas under subparagraph 10 of that Article;
2. Projects specified in the subparagraphs of Article 10 (1) of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Establishment and Promotion of Use of Smart Grids;
3. Other projects requested by the Integrated Special City Mayor or deemed necessary by the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment to promote the supply and use of renewable energy within energy self-sufficient cities.

Article 62 (Procedures and Methods for Supporting Electricity Grid Construction to Promote Distributed Energy)
(1) To receive support under Article 235 (1) of the Act, the Integrated Special City Mayor shall submit a project plan containing the following matters to the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment:
1. The name, purpose, and necessity of the project;
2. The location, scope, and implementation period of the project;
3. The project implementer and relevant institutions;
4. Authorizations and permits, consultations, or administrative support necessary for the project;
5. Measures for carrying out the project, including connection to the power system and installation of electricity facilities or power lines;
6. A financing plan and expected effects;
7. Other matters deemed necessary by the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment to examine whether to provide support.
(2) After reviewing the project plan under paragraph (1), the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment may, in consultation with relevant institutions, formulate administrative support measures relating to the following matters:
