1. Consolidated consultation on and expedited handling of authorization and permit procedures among relevant administrative agencies;
2. Use of sites held by the State, local governments, or public institutions;
3. Consultation and coordination among relevant institutions regarding connection to the power system;
4. Administrative support for applying regulatory exceptions or undertaking demonstration projects under relevant statutes and regulations;
5. Other administrative support deemed necessary by the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment to promote distributed energy.
(3) "The scope prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 235 (3) of the Act means the following matters:
1. Procedures for applying for support;
2. Methods for preparing project plans;
3. Criteria and priorities for selecting recipients of support;
4. Procedures for consultation with relevant institutions;
5. Other matters necessary to reflect the characteristics of projects within the Integrated Special City.

Article 63 (Payment of Grid Usage Fees)
(1) Grid usage fees under Article 235 (4) of the Act shall be calculated taking into account the following matters:
1. Electricity grid construction costs;
2. Costs of operating, maintaining, and repairing the electricity grid;
3. Costs of using shared connection facilities connected to the electricity grid (limited to facilities installed by a transmission business operator or distribution business operator under Article 2, subparagraph 6 or 8 of the Electric Utility Act);
4. Other costs recognized by the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment as directly related to expansion of the electricity grid.
(2) When calculating grid usage fees pursuant to paragraph (1), the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment may reduce or exempt such fees, comprehensively taking into account the following matters:
1. Whether the use of distributed energy increases social and economic benefits through reductions in transmission grid installation costs, avoidance of social conflicts, stabilization of electricity supply, and other effects;
2. Whether attracting large-scale electricity demand, such as semiconductor facilities and data centers, to the Integrated Special City contributes to stabilizing national electricity supply and demand;
3. Whether the project is a power generation project involving resident participation or a project in which the Integrated Special City and local public enterprises have directly invested pursuant to Article 238 of the Act;
4. Other matters for which the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment deems reduction or exemption of grid usage fees necessary to promote distributed energy.
(3) Matters necessary concerning the imposition criteria, calculation methods, reduction and exemption rates, payment procedures, and payment timing for grid usage fees shall be determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment.

Article 64 (Special Cases concerning Investments and Corporate Bond Issuance by Local Public Enterprises for New and Renewable Energy Businesses)
Pursuant to Article 241 (4) 1 of the Act, projects specified in the following subparagraphs shall be excluded from the feasibility reviews specified in the respective subparagraphs:
1. Projects for which the investment amount is less than the amount specified in the proviso to Article 47-2 (1) of the Enforcement Decree of the Local Public Enterprises Act: Feasibility reviews under Article 54 of that Act;
2. Projects for which the total project cost is less than the amount specified in Article 25-3 (1) 1 of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Management of Public Institutions: Feasibility reviews under Article 65-3 of the Local Public Enterprises Act.

Article 65 (Support for Semiconductor Industry Specialized Complexes, etc.)
(1) The criteria for supporting costs under the portion of Article 250 (3) of the Act preceding the subparagraphs and the detailed scope of industrial infrastructure under subparagraphs 1 through 5 of that paragraph shall be governed by Article 14 of the Special Act on Strengthening the Competitiveness of and Supporting the Semiconductor Industry: Provided, That the specific scope and scale of support may be determined through consultation between the head of the central administrative agency and the Integrated Special City Mayor.
(2) When determining the specific scope and scale of support pursuant to the proviso to paragraph (1), the head of the central administrative agency and the Integrated Special City Mayor may give priority to projects in which two or more Si/Gun/Gu cooperate to develop a semiconductor industry specialized complex in order to promote industrial clustering across regions.
(3) Articles 31 and 32 of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on Special Measures for Strengthening and Protecting the Competitiveness of National High-Tech Strategic Industries shall apply mutatis mutandis to matters necessary for supporting the development and operation of semiconductor industry specialized complexes and the installation and management of industrial infrastructure, other than those prescribed in paragraph (1).

Article 66 (Support for Developing New Industries Linking the Semiconductor and Defense Industries)
(1) The scope of support for developing new industries linking the semiconductor and defense industries under Article 251 (1) of the Act shall be as follows:
1. Planning and implementation of research and development projects for technology development, technology introduction, and technological advancement in fields linking the semiconductor and defense industries, and support necessary therefor;
2. Support for establishing and operating cooperative systems to promote joint research, technology transfer, commercialization, and information exchange among businesses, universities, research institutes, and support institutions related to the semiconductor and defense industries;
3. Support for testing, evaluation, demonstration, standardization, and infrastructure development to secure foundational technologies in fields linking the semiconductor and defense industries and use them industrially;
4. Support for operating programs for the training of specialized personnel, education and training, field training, and strengthening the capabilities of incumbent workers necessary for developing new industries linking the semiconductor and defense industries;
5. Support for entering domestic and overseas markets, connecting with demand, developing sales channels, and promoting commercialization;
6. Other matters equivalent to the support specified in subparagraphs 1 through 5 that the competent minister deems necessary, in consultation with the heads of relevant central administrative agencies, to promote the development of new industries linking the semiconductor and defense industries.
(2) To efficiently provide support under paragraph (1), the State may provide relevant institutions or organizations with all or part of the costs necessary to carry out such projects within budgetary limits.

Article 67 (Support for Promoting the Secondary Battery Industry)
(1) The State shall implement and support the following matters pursuant to Article 261 (1) and (2) of the Act:
1. Formulation and implementation of policies for technology development, commercialization, and expansion of the industrial ecosystem in the secondary battery industry;
2. Support for joint research, technology transfer, demonstration, and the establishment and operation of cooperative systems among businesses, universities, research institutes, and support institutions related to the secondary battery industry;
3. Support for promoting domestic investment, expansion of facilities, and clustering of businesses related to the secondary battery industry;
4. Support for the installation, expansion, or improvement of infrastructure necessary to promote the secondary battery industry;
5. Support for training specialized personnel, education and training, and strengthening the capabilities of incumbent workers related to the secondary battery industry;
6. Support for testing, evaluation, certification, standardization, and demonstration projects to strengthen the competitiveness of the secondary battery industry;
7. Financial support and support for cooperation among relevant institutions to efficiently carry out the support projects specified in subparagraphs 1 through 6;
8. Other matters equivalent to the projects specified in subparagraphs 1 through 7 that the Minister of Trade and Industry deems necessary, in consultation with the heads of relevant central administrative agencies, to promote the secondary battery industry.
(2) To efficiently carry out the support projects under paragraph (1), the State may provide relevant institutions or organizations with all or part of the necessary costs within budgetary limits.

SECTION 3 AGRICULTURE, FORESTRY AND FISHERIES, TALENT DEVELOPMENT, AND WELFARE

Article 68 (Formulation of Fishing Ground and Licensed Aquaculture Ground Use and Development Plans)
(1) Pursuant to Article 281 (2) of the Act, by January 31 of the year in which a fishing ground use and development plan under Article 4 (1) of the Fisheries Act and a licensed aquaculture ground use and development plan under Article 9 (1) of the Aquaculture Industry Development Act (hereinafter referred to as "fishing ground and licensed aquaculture ground use and development plans") are to be formulated, the Integrated Special City Mayor shall prepare detailed guidelines for such development plans (hereinafter referred to as "detailed guidelines") in accordance with the basic guidelines for development plans under Article 4 (3) of the Fisheries Act and Article 9 (2) of the Aquaculture Industry Development Act, and notify the heads of Si and Gun within the Mayor's jurisdiction thereof.
(2) In accordance with the detailed guidelines, the heads of Si and Gun shall, by March 31 each year, formulate fishing ground and licensed aquaculture ground use and development plans for the period from July 1 of that year to June 30 of the following year and submit them to the Integrated Special City Mayor.
(3) Where the heads of Si and Gun intend to grant fishing licenses or aquaculture licenses for the following waters when formulating fishing ground and licensed aquaculture ground use and development plans pursuant to paragraph (2), they shall reflect such licenses in those plans:
1. Waters for which the validity period of a fishing license under Article 14 of the Fisheries Act or an aquaculture license under Article 17 of the Aquaculture Industry Development Act expires during the period from July 1 of that year to June 30 of the following year;
2. Waters for which a person who has acquired an aquaculture right under Article 2, subparagraph 8 of the Aquaculture Industry Development Act intends to relinquish that aquaculture right pursuant to Article 22 (5) of that Act.
(4) The Integrated Special City Mayor shall examine whether fishing ground and licensed aquaculture ground use and development plans under paragraph (2) conform to the detailed guidelines and notify the heads of Si and Gun of the results by April 30 each year.

Article 69 (Scope of Special Admissions for Local Talent)
"The scope prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the main clause of Article 314 (1) of the Act means the following matters:
1. The department shall be a specialized department operated in connection with regional strategic industries (meaning high-tech industries specified in the subparagraphs of Article 185 of the Act; hereinafter the same shall apply) and designated in accordance with criteria prescribed by Integrated Special City Ordinance;
2. Eligible applicants shall be persons who have graduated or are expected to graduate from a high school under Article 45 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act located within the jurisdiction of the Integrated Special City (including broadcasting and correspondence high schools attached to high schools pursuant to Article 51 of that Act);
3. The number of persons selected shall be within 50 percent of the admission quota of the relevant admissions unit.

Article 70 (Special Cases concerning Links between Regional Hub Campuses of National Universities and Strategic Industries)
(1) The head of a national university having jurisdiction over a regional hub campus of a national university may apply to the Minister of Education for regulatory exceptions under Article 59-10 of the Higher Education Act (hereinafter referred to as "regulatory exceptions" in this Article) to strengthen links with regional strategic industries and new industries pursuant to Article 341 (1) of the Act.
(2) Upon receiving an application under paragraph (1), the Minister of Education shall notify the heads of relevant administrative agencies of its contents and deliberate on whether to grant regulatory exceptions, including consideration of reviews by the relevant administrative agencies.
(3) Where an extension of an approved period of regulatory exceptions is necessary, the Minister of Education may evaluate operational performance and feasibility and take necessary measures, such as extending the period or revoking approval.
(4) Matters necessary for regulatory exceptions, other than those prescribed in paragraphs (1) through (3), shall be governed by Articles 59-10 through 59-12 of the Higher Education Act.

Article 71 (Scope of Use for Fisheries and Marine Education and Research)
(1) Notwithstanding Article 46 of the Fisheries Act, Article 45 of the Fishing Villages and Fishery Harbors Act, and Article 53 of the Aquaculture Industry Development Act, the Integrated Special City Mayor may, pursuant to Article 341 (2) of the Act, approve field training, tests, or demonstrations by regional hub campuses of national universities at the following locations for fisheries and marine education, research, and links with industry:
1. Fishing grounds;
2. Aquaculture grounds;
3. Ports and fishery harbors;
4. Coastal areas.
(2) Field training, tests, or demonstrations under paragraph (1) may be operated in connection with the following courses and programs:
1. Education in degree programs;
2. Curricula linked with industry;
3. Retraining courses for persons working in the fisheries and marine industries;
4. Programs for training research and development personnel.
(3) Specific matters necessary for use for educational and research purposes under paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be determined by the Minister of Education in consultation with the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries.

Article 72 (Special Cases concerning Housing Supply for Outstanding Talent)
(1) Where the Integrated Special City Mayor supplies housing constructed and offered within the jurisdiction of the Integrated Special City to outstanding talent in fields of future new industries determined by the Mayor pursuant to the main clause of Article 344 (1) of the Act, the Mayor may provide a special supply on a one-time basis, limited to one housing unit per household.
(2) Eligibility for occupancy of and methods for selecting occupants of housing specially supplied pursuant to paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City Ordinance.
(3) "Areas where speculation is a concern, as prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the proviso to Article 344 (1) of the Act means the following areas:
1. Designated areas under Article 104-2 (1) of the Income Tax Act;
2. Overheated speculation districts under Article 63 of the Housing Act;
3. Areas subject to adjustment under Article 63-2 of the Housing Act.

SECTION 4 OTHER MATTERS

Article 73 (Special Cases concerning Reductions of or Exemptions from Fees for Use of State or Public Land, etc.)
(1) "Common facilities and facility modernization projects prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 348 of the Act means common facilities under Article 18 (2) of the Special Act on the Promotion of Traditional Markets and Shopping Districts and facility modernization projects under Article 20 (1) of that Act.
(2) Where the Government and the Integrated Special City Mayor intend to reduce or exempt usage fees or lease fees pursuant to Article 348 of the Act, they shall apply the reduction or exemption rates in the following categories:
1. In the case of State property: 80 percent of the usage fee under Article 29 of the Enforcement Decree of the State Property Act;
2. In the case of public property: A reduction or exemption rate prescribed by Integrated Special City Ordinance within 80 percent of the usage fee or lease fee under Article 14 or 31 of the Enforcement Decree of the Public Property and Commodity Management Act.

Article 74 (Support for Promoting the Tourism Industry in Areas with Declining Populations)
(1) Projects eligible for support for promoting the tourism industry under Article 360 (3) of the Act shall be as follows:
1. Projects to develop tourism resources using resources distinctive to the region;
2. Projects to improve the convenience of travel for tourism;
3. Publicity and marketing projects to attract tourists;
4. Projects to support the establishment and operation of tourism businesses;
5. Projects to promote tourism enterprises;
6. Projects to train specialized personnel in the tourism industry;
7. Other projects deemed necessary by the Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism to promote the tourism industry in areas with declining populations and areas of concern for population decline under Article 2, subparagraphs 1 and 1-2 of the Special Act on Support for Areas with Declining Populations.
(2) The scope of support under Article 360 (3) of the Act shall be as follows:
1. Loans to tourism business operators for establishment and operating funds;
2. Support for domestic and overseas tourism marketing and publicity to attract tourists;
3. Support for training tourism professionals and for education and consulting;
4. Other administrative and financial support necessary to promote the tourism industry.

Article 75 (Areas in Which Special Cases for Foreign Cultural and Artistic Professionals and Tourism Industry Workers Apply)
"Districts and special zones prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 363 of the Act means the following districts, special zones, and other areas:
1. Cultural districts under Article 18 (1) of the Regional Culture Promotion Act;
2. Cultural industry promotion districts under Article 28-2 (1) of the Framework Act on the Promotion of Cultural Industries;
3. Areas with declining populations under Article 2, subparagraph 12 of the Special Act on Local Autonomy, Decentralization, and Balanced Growth;
4. Free economic zones under Article 4 (4) of the Special Act on Designation and Management of Free Economic Zones;
5. Investment promotion districts under Article 16 (1) of the Special Act on the Creation of an Asian Culture Hub City;
6. Tourist destinations, tourist complexes, or special tourism zones under Article 52 (1) or 70 (1) of the Tourism Promotion Act.

Article 76 (Hearing Opinions When Formulating Development Plans for Forest Use Promotion Districts)
(1) Where the Integrated Special City Mayor intends to hear the opinions of the competent heads of Si/Gun/Gu on a promotion district development plan under Article 381 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as a "promotion district development plan") pursuant to paragraph (3) of that Article, the Mayor shall require the heads of Si/Gun/Gu to submit written opinions on the direction of development of the relevant area and the development projects and other measures necessary therefor.
(2) Where the Integrated Special City Mayor intends to hear the opinions of local residents and experts pursuant to Article 381 (3) of the Act, the Mayor shall prepare a draft promotion district development plan and publicly announce its principal contents in the official bulletin, on the website of the Integrated Special City, and through other means.
(3) The heads of Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over a draft promotion district development plan under paragraph (2) shall make the draft plan available for public inspection for at least 14 days.
(4) A person who has an opinion on the contents of a draft promotion district development plan publicly announced pursuant to paragraph (2) may submit a written opinion to the Integrated Special City Mayor or the competent head of Si/Gun/Gu during the inspection period under paragraph (3).
(5) The Integrated Special City Mayor or the competent head of Si/Gun/Gu who receives written opinions pursuant to paragraph (4) shall prepare a written review opinion. In such cases, the Integrated Special City Mayor may have the competent heads of Si/Gun/Gu prepare written review opinions.
(6) The heads of Si/Gun/Gu shall submit the written opinions received pursuant to paragraph (4) and the written review opinions under paragraph (5) to the Integrated Special City Mayor.

Article 77 (Designation of Implementers of Forest Use Promotion Projects)
"Public institutions prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 383 (1) 2 of the Act means the following public institutions:
1. The Korea Land and Housing Corporation under the Korea Land and Housing Corporation Act;
2. The Korea Railroad Corporation under the Korea Railroad Corporation Act;
3. The Korea National Railway under the Korea National Railway Act;
4. The Korea Tourism Organization under the Korea Tourism Organization Act;
5. The Korea Rural Community Corporation under the Korea Rural Community Corporation and Farmland Management Fund Act;
6. The Korea Racing Authority under the Korea Racing Authority Act;
7. The Korea Forest Welfare Institute under the Forestry Welfare Promotion Act;
8. The Korea Arboreta and Gardens Institute under the Act on the Creation and Promotion of Arboretums and Gardens;
9. The Korea Forestry Promotion Institute under the Forestry and Mountain Villages Development Promotion Act;
10. The Korea Mountaineering and Trekking Support Center under the Forestry Culture and Recreation Act;
11. The Korea Forest Disaster Safety Technology Corporation under the Forest Disaster Prevention Act.

Article 78 (Special Cases concerning Application of the Mountainous Districts Management Act and Other Acts within Promotion Districts)
(1) For a forest use promotion project, notwithstanding Article 12 of the Mountainous Districts Management Act, conversion or temporary use of mountainous districts may be undertaken pursuant to Article 386 (1) of the Act to perform the following acts in conservation mountainous districts under Article 4 (1) 1 of the Mountainous Districts Management Act (excluding areas in which conversion or temporary use of mountainous districts is restricted under Article 9 (1) of that Act):
1. Acts falling under any subparagraph of Article 12 (1) or (2) of the Mountainous Districts Management Act;
2. Installation of facilities necessary for a forest use promotion project included in a promotion district development plan;
3. Installation of facilities necessary for a tourism business under Article 2, subparagraph 1 of the Tourism Promotion Act.
(2) The criteria for permission for conversion of mountainous districts concerning the slope and elevation of mountainous districts for forest use promotion projects under Article 386 (1) of the Act shall be as follows:
1. Slope: Notwithstanding subparagraph 2 (c) 1) (a) and (b) of attached Table 4 of the Enforcement Decree of the Mountainous Districts Management Act, the average slope of the mountainous district to be converted shall satisfy all of the following criteria:
(a) The average slope of the mountainous district to be converted shall be 35 degrees or less;
(b) Where the mountainous district to be converted is divided into areas of 100 square meters and the slope of each area is measured, the area with a slope of 35 degrees or more shall not exceed 40 percent of the total area: Provided, That this shall not apply where facilities for a ski resort business under Article 10 (1) 1 of the Installation and Utilization of Sports Facilities Act are installed.
2. Elevation: Notwithstanding subparagraph 1 (e) 6) of attached Table 4 of the Enforcement Decree of the Mountainous Districts Management Act, to preserve the landscape of the mountainous district, the mountainous district to be converted shall be located at a height of less than 80 percent of the elevation of the relevant mountainous district.
(3) "Forest public-interest facilities prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 386 (2) 2 of the Act means the following facilities:
1. Forest campsites under Article 2, subparagraph 8 of the Forestry Culture and Recreation Act (limited to campsites with an area of 30,000 square meters or less);
2. Forest leisure sports facilities under Article 2, subparagraph 9 of the Forestry Culture and Recreation Act (excluding mountain skiing facilities, hang-gliding facilities, and paragliding facilities).

Article 79 (Support for Infrastructure Installation, etc.)
(1) "Facilities prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as roads" in Article 387 (1) of the Act means infrastructure under Article 2, subparagraph 6 of the National Land Planning and Utilization Act.
(2) Pursuant to Article 387 (1) of the Act, the State and the Integrated Special City may give priority to installing the following facilities among the infrastructure under paragraph (1) of this Article or supporting their installation costs:
1. Transportation facilities, such as roads, rail tracks, and parking lots;
2. Distribution and supply facilities, such as water, electricity, and gas supply equipment and broadcasting and telecommunications facilities;
3. Basic environmental facilities, such as sewerage, waste treatment and recycling facilities, and water pollution prevention facilities;
4. Other facilities deemed necessary by the Integrated Special City Mayor for the smooth implementation of forest use promotion projects and the attraction of investment.

Article 80 (Implementation of Projects for the Preservation of National Heritage within Historical and Cultural Special Zones, etc.)
(1) Where the Integrated Special City Mayor intends to undertake a project pursuant to Article 392 (3) of the Act, the Mayor shall formulate a plan therefor, publicly announce its contents in the official bulletin, on the website of the Integrated Special City, and through other means, and make it available for public inspection for at least 14 days.
(2) A person who has an opinion on a draft plan publicly announced pursuant to paragraph (1) may submit a written opinion to the Integrated Special City Mayor during the inspection period.
(3) The Integrated Special City Mayor shall prepare a written review opinion on the opinions submitted pursuant to paragraph (2) and decide whether to reflect them in the relevant plan.

Article 81 (Special Cases concerning Preservation and Utilization of Nationally Designated Heritage within Historical and Cultural Special Zones, etc.)
(1) A person who intends to perform an act falling under any subparagraph of Article 21-2 (2) of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Preservation and Utilization of Cultural Heritage (excluding an act under subparagraph 1 (a) of that paragraph) for any of the following activities shall obtain permission from the Integrated Special City Mayor pursuant to Article 393 (1) of the Act, notwithstanding the main clause of Article 35 (1) of the Act on the Preservation and Utilization of Cultural Heritage. In such cases, the Integrated Special City Mayor shall consult with the Administrator of the Korea Heritage Service before granting permission.
1. Traditional performances organized by the State or a local government;
2. Operation of experiential programs using cultural heritage;
3. Events recreating historical facts associated with cultural heritage;
4. Operation of educational programs using cultural heritage.
(2) Pursuant to Article 393 (1) of the Act, the Integrated Special City Mayor may support the following projects within historical and cultural special zones to protect and promote national intangible heritage designated pursuant to Article 12 (1) of the Act on the Preservation and Promotion of Intangible Heritage:
1. Support for activities to transmit intangible heritage and education in its transmission;
2. Surveys, research, and documentation of intangible heritage;
3. Performances, exhibitions, and development of cultural content using intangible heritage.
(3) The Integrated Special City Mayor may decide whether to provide support under paragraph (2) in consultation with the consultative body under Article 392 (4) of the Act.

Article 82 (Special Cases concerning State Property and Public Property within Historical and Cultural Special Zones)
(1) "Persons prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 393 (2) of the Act means the following persons:
1. Public institutions under Article 4 of the Act on the Management of Public Institutions;
2. Local public corporations or local public agencies established pursuant to Article 49 or 76 of the Local Public Enterprises Act;
3. Non-profit corporations established under the Civil Act or other Acts that the Integrated Special City Mayor has designated as implementers of projects to create historical and cultural special zones.
(2) Use of, and derivation of profits from, State property or public property by negotiated contract pursuant to Article 393 (2) of the Act shall be allowed only where all of the following requirements are satisfied:
1. Such use shall be directly necessary for the creation or operation of a historical and cultural special zone;
2. It shall be difficult to achieve the purpose of the project without the relevant property;
3. The scope of use and derivation of profits shall be limited to the minimum necessary.
(3) A person seeking the application of special provisions to State property pursuant to Article 393 (2) of the Act shall apply to the head of the competent central government agency, attaching a written opinion of the Integrated Special City Mayor. In such cases, the head of the competent central government agency may, in consultation with the Integrated Special City Mayor, decide whether to grant permission to use and derive profits from the State property or to reduce or exempt usage fees.
(4) A person seeking the application of special provisions to public property pursuant to Article 393 (2) of the Act shall apply to the Integrated Special City Mayor. In such cases, the Integrated Special City Mayor may decide to grant permission to use and derive profits from the public property or to reduce or exempt usage fees in accordance with relevant statutes and regulations.
(5) Reductions of or exemptions from usage fees under paragraphs (3) and (4) may be granted only within the scope prescribed by relevant statutes and regulations, and no reduction or exemption shall be granted for portions used for sales, business operations, leasing, advertising, or other profit-making businesses.
(6) Matters concerning permission to use and derive profits from State property or public property, the period of use, management, revocation, and other matters, other than those prescribed in paragraphs (2) through (5), shall be governed by the State Property Act, the Public Property and Commodity Management Act, and other relevant statutes and regulations.
